clue.text: Revelations I can make about what young men used to do

definitions.text: what young men used to do

indicators.note: to make something about is to turn it round and remake it, so the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A biblical reader wonders what to make of the Book of Revelation's message about the habits of young men of old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make about' rearranges the fifteen letters of REVELATIONS I CAN. Compulsory military service for young British men ended in 1960.
explanation.definitionFit: Compulsory military duty was a stint that British young men once had to serve, ending around 1960.

clue.text: Parts of bodies which have their point during sleep

indicators.note: one thing happening during another sits inside it, so the point goes within the sleep

parts.note: naps are short sleeps
E (east) is a compass point

explanation.surface: Body parts that come to a point while their owner dozes.
explanation.definitionFit: The backs of necks are parts of the body.

clue.text: To half study a thinker is drudgery

indicators.note: half of a two-letter word is just its first letter, so only part of the word To is kept

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it
John Stuart Mill was a philosopher

explanation.surface: Half-heartedly studying a philosopher feels like a chore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' keeps T of TO; to READ a subject at university is to study it, and MILL is the philosopher J S Mill.
explanation.definitionFit: A wearisome routine of monotonous work, like walking a mill wheel endlessly, is drudgery.

clue.text: Accomplish about four climbs as a poet

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means the letters read from bottom to top, so backwards
about means surrounding, so the first word goes round the second

parts.note: to accomplish something is to do it
IV is the Roman numeral for four

explanation.surface: Achieving roughly four climbs makes one a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts IV inside DO to give DIVO; 'climbs' turns that upward in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Publius Ovidius Naso, author of the Metamorphoses, was a Roman poet.

clue.text: Give the gang some weapons and something to wear

parts.note: to give someone weapons is to arm them, the verb sense
a band is a group or gang of people

explanation.surface: Supplying the mob with guns, and a bit of clothing besides.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as an instruction: 'arm the band'. ARM is the verb meaning to give weapons, so 'some weapons' only fills out the sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip of cloth worn round the sleeve is an item of attire.

clue.text: Time for rises

definitions.meaning: springtime, the season, plural for seasons year after year
a verb: jumps up or leaps upward

explanation.definitionFit: The vernal season is a time of year, and the verb sense means leaps upward or rises suddenly.

clue.text: Revelled when tories turned socialist

indicators.note: turned means the word tories is turned around and its letters reordered

parts.note: red is a colour and label for a socialist or left-winger

explanation.surface: Conservatives partied after converting to socialism.
explanation.definitionFit: To carouse noisily is to make merry, a synonym of revelling.

clue.text: Woman seen to be in dire need

indicators.note: the name can be seen sitting inside the phrase dire need, spanning its two words

explanation.surface: A woman spotted in desperate want.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a female first name, so stands for a woman.

clue.text: Restaurant discovers source of wealth in unusual taste

indicators.note: in puts the mine inside the rearranged letters
unusual tells us the word taste is made odd by rearranging its letters

parts.note: a mine is a source of riches, literally or figuratively

explanation.surface: A diner unearths a gold mine of quirky flavours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges TASTE as ESTAT; 'in' puts MINE inside, after ESTA.
explanation.definitionFit: A small French cafe or bistro selling drinks and food is an estaminet.

clue.text: A prize given before mother embraces one

parts.note: pre- is a prefix meaning before

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold within, so mother surrounds one

parts.note: mum is an informal word for mother
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An award handed out before mother hugs someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonus or reward is a prize, as in a prize paid at a premium.

clue.text: Clothes torn without a purpose

indicators.note: without here is the old sense outside, so torn goes around a purpose

parts.note: rent is the past participle of rend, meaning torn
an aim is a purpose

explanation.surface: Ripped clothing worn pointlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' in its old sense of 'outside' puts RENT around AIM, not the usual 'lacking'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an archaic, literary word for garments or attire.

clue.text: Team composed of stars but without real finish

indicators.note: without means the word real is taken away from what comes before
finish says the removed word real comes off the end

parts.note: sidereal means relating to or made of the stars
taken as written

explanation.surface: A team full of stars, though none really finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: SIDEREAL means 'of the stars'; 'without' and 'finish' take the REAL off its end.
explanation.definitionFit: A side is a team in sport, as in a football eleven.

clue.text: Chief master turning out to be normal

parts.note: main means chief or principal

indicators.note: turning out signals the word master is turned inside out and reshaped

explanation.surface: A head teacher proves to be ordinary after all.
explanation.definitionFit: Conventional or ordinary views and tastes are those of the majority current.

clue.text: Hurried round the edge and lost footing

indicators.note: round means the first word goes around the second

parts.note: sped means hurried
a lip is the edge or rim of something

explanation.surface: Someone running round the rim lost their footing.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose one's footing is to slide and fall, a synonym phrase.

clue.text: Kind of poisoning which shows a revolution exists in the writing up

indicators.note: in puts the revolution phrase inside the writing
in a down light, up means the letters are read upward, so backwards

parts.note: MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing
a turn is a revolution
is means exists

explanation.surface: A kind of poisoning revealed by a revolution in the writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses MS to SM; 'in' places A TURN IS inside it. Saturn was the alchemists' name for lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead poisoning takes its name from Saturn, the alchemical symbol for lead.

clue.text: Blissful and is nearly all after the unfinished display

indicators.note: after means the following pieces come after the display
unfinished means the last letter of the word for display is cut off

parts.note: a parade is a display or show
taken as written

indicators.note: nearly means not quite the whole word, so its last letter is lost

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Joy comes almost entirely after a half-done show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' cuts PARADE to PARAD and 'nearly' cuts ALL to AL; 'after' places IS + AL behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavenly or idyllic, like Eden, means supremely happy.

clue.text: Tried hard when a gun holds the right woman back

indicators.note: holds means the gun contains the following letters

parts.note: the Sten is a British submachine gun

indicators.note: back means the woman's name is read in reverse

parts.note: Vi is a woman's name, short for Violet

explanation.surface: A gunman struggled when holding the right woman back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns VI into IV; 'holds' puts R + IV inside STEN after ST.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the past participle of strive, meaning made a great effort.

clue.text: Food which is obtainable after the end of the war

indicators.note: after puts obtainable behind the end of the war

parts.note: VE Day marked victory in Europe, the end of the Second World War there
getable means able to be obtained

explanation.surface: Food becomes available once the war is over.
explanation.walkthrough: VE stands for Victory in Europe, 8 May 1945. 'the end of the war' looks like a final letter R, but it is the date.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant grown to be eaten, such as a carrot, is a food.

clue.text: A trail falsely leading to a means of flight

indicators.note: leading to places the rearranged letters before the final a
falsely means the letters of a trail are set out wrongly

explanation.surface: A false trail leads to an escape route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falsely' rearranges A TRAIL as TALARI; 'leading to' puts it before the second A.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth Hermes wore winged sandals that let him fly through the air.

clue.text: A medical man's highest card is the lowest throw

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor; the possessive adds S
the ace is the top card in many games

explanation.surface: A doctor's top card turns out to be the worst roll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'medical man' is MB with the possessive S. In dice, a pair of aces is the lowest possible throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Double ace, scoring two, is the poorest roll with two dice.

clue.text: Adorned a man found in a bay

indicators.note: found in means the man is located inside the bay

parts.note: a bight is a curving bay of coastline
Ed is a man's name, short for Edward

explanation.surface: Someone decorated a man discovered in a cove.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for decked out or arrayed, meaning ornamented.

clue.text: A tough guy who has little weight inside him

definitions.text: A tough guy who has little weight inside him

parts.words: A tough guy who has little weight inside him
parts.note: a nightclub doorman is a hard man, and his title holds the name of a small unit of weight within it

explanation.surface: A muscleman who is, oddly, a lightweight inside.
explanation.walkthrough: A cryptic definition: the doorman's title has OUNCE, a little weight, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorman who ejects troublemakers from a club is a tough heavy.

clue.text: If one has drinks before a fight it makes one slow down

indicators.note: before puts the drinks ahead of the fight

parts.note: a round is a set of drinks bought for a group
a bout is a fight, as in boxing

explanation.surface: A drinker who stands a round before a scrap ends up slowing down.
explanation.walkthrough: A ROUND is drinks for the whole group, bought in turn in British pubs; a traffic circle makes drivers slow down.
explanation.definitionFit: A traffic circle at a junction forces approaching drivers to reduce speed.

clue.text: Part of cow shivered without shed

indicators.note: without means the letters of shed are removed from the word for shivered

parts.note: shuddered means shivered
taken as written, its letters scattered at the two ends

explanation.surface: A cow shook outside, having no barn.
explanation.walkthrough: SH comes off the front and ED off the back of SHUDDERED.
explanation.definitionFit: The milk-producing organ of a cow is part of it.

clue.text: Hits back to cause injury

indicators.note: back means the word for hits is read in reverse

parts.note: bats means hits, as with a bat

explanation.surface: Striking back to hurt someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce with a knife is to wound, causing injury.

clue.text: Cap which is right in the middle of the vegetables

indicators.note: in the middle of puts right at the centre of the vegetable word

parts.note: beet, used as a mass noun, covers the root vegetables

explanation.surface: A hat sitting right in the middle of the veg patch.
explanation.definitionFit: A round flat soft hat, as worn by French artists, is a cap.

clue.text: Piece of furniture which is not quite as remote

indicators.note: not quite means the phrase loses its final letter

parts.note: so far means as remote or distant

explanation.surface: A furnishing that is not quite so distant.
explanation.definitionFit: A couch is an upholstered seat for several people.

clue.text: They offer protection for us in a big country

indicators.note: in puts us inside the big country

parts.note: India is a large country

explanation.surface: Defences for us in a vast nation.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany and zoology these are protective membranes or coverings, such as those over fern spore clusters.

clue.text: The lever is caught with line and rod

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a row is a line
a bar is a rod

explanation.surface: The handle is snagged on fishing line and rod.
explanation.definitionFit: An iron bar used for prising is a lever.

clue.text: Movement which makes rear alarm change within short time

indicators.note: within puts the rearranged letters inside the short time

parts.note: a moment is a short time

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of the letters of rear alarm

explanation.surface: A campaign that turns a rear alarm into a change of heart in a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges REAR ALARM as RALREARMA; 'within' puts it inside MOMENT after MO. Moral Re-Armament was a 20th-century religious and moral movement.
explanation.definitionFit: It was an international moral and spiritual campaign founded by Frank Buchman in 1938.
